heading: Friday, October 3, 2025
topLine: Diffusion model pinpoints a new antibiotic's target, cutting a two-year study to six months.

items.headline: Diffusion model pinpoints a new antibiotic's target, cutting a two-year study to six months
items.summary: McMaster and MIT researchers used the generative docking model DiffDock to predict in minutes that the narrow-spectrum antibiotic enterololin binds the LolCDE lipoprotein-transport complex; resistant-mutant sequencing, RNA-seq and CRISPR knockdowns confirmed the prediction, and the drug spared the wider microbiome in mouse models of Crohn's-like inflammation. Published in Nature; the team says mechanism-of-action work that normally takes 18 months to two years took about six months.
